verify.note: This file replaces an earlier round-1 design review that was written against an older build (490-unit figures, 33 min read, light-theme callout output contrast bug). Those three problems are no longer present in the current build: figures are 350 units wide and legible on a phone, the header says 22 min read, and output panels inside callouts render correctly in light theme.

comparedAgainst: https://www.atlassian.com/data/sql/sql-join-types-explained-visually (fetched; the fetcher returned navigation only, not used for scoring)
justification: Real numbers from report.json / lighthouse.json: Lighthouse 97 / 100 / 100 / 100 on the first run (no re-run needed), 0 console errors, 0 console warnings, 0 broken links, 0 px mobile overflow; the only verify failure is the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder. As a designed page this is clearly ahead of the ranking results I read. Coding Horror is a ~1,300-word post built on the very Venn diagrams this article argues against, with two four-row tables and no treatment of NULL keys, ON-vs-WHERE or row multiplication. Microsoft Learn's joins page is a 4,000-word reference with plain-text result listings, no row-level figure, and most of its length on physical operators. Ours has an excellent rhythm: the longest prose run is about seven desktop lines, nearly every query is followed at once by a terminal-style RESULT panel, and the hook (three attempts at one report) is shown, not told. The four figures (match lines, the 4x5 pair grid, the bracket figure for INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL, the crossed loan/payment lines) are informative rather than decorative, sit on 350-unit canvases that are legible at 390 px, swap amber/green/red tokens correctly in dark theme, and have captions that say what to notice. Headings are specific and content-led, the single h3 nests correctly in the TOC, callouts are restrained (one pitfall, one .NET), and exercise solutions are collapsed. It does not reach 8.5 because several binding phone/exercise rules from the editorial brief are broken in ways a reader will see: Exercise 1 prints its own answer under a 'without running it' prompt; on a 390 px phone the operative half of roughly ten code lines and two result panels is clipped (both EXISTS correlations, the NOT IN subquery, the `owes` expression and both join conditions of the fix query, the C# `if` that implements ON, the `amount` column of the row-multiplication result, the `null_is_null` column); Figure 4 does not exist (numbering jumps 3 to 5) and Figure 5 has two column labels colliding into 'payment_idamount' in every viewport; the NOT IN expansion is a 50-character inline code run that wraps raggedly; and the page closes with the banned 'Exercises' heading + 'Predict the ...' first item. All of these are one-round writer fixes; with them done this is an 8.5-9 page.

issues.fixLooksLike: Move the query's `text output` block (or the whole query/output pair, keeping them adjacent so run-code still verifies it) inside the :::solution. The prompt then shows only the query. Exercise 2 may keep its visible result because the wrong output is part of the question.

issues.problem: Blocks scroll inside their own box (no page overflow), but the part that is cut off at the fade is repeatedly the part the prose is about, which the brief's phone rule forbids. Worst cases: (a) both EXISTS queries show 'SELECT 1 FROM loan AS l WHERE l.member_' with the correlation hidden; (b) the NOT IN trap shows 'NOT IN (SELECT member_i'; (c) the fix query hides the entire `- COALESCE(paid.total, 0) AS owes` expression and the right-hand side of both `LEFT JOIN ... ON` lines; (d) the row-multiplication RESULT is 41 columns and its last column, `amount`, the one being double-summed, is the one clipped; (e) the NULL comparison RESULT is 43 columns and `null_is_null`, the contrast case, is clipped; (f) in the C# program the members/loans initializers, the LeftJoin signature, the explanatory comment and the key line `if (l.MemberId is int id && id == m.Id)` are all cut; (g) in the .NET callout (narrower still) the `left.Join(right, l => l, ...)` call and both WriteLine strings are cut; (h) minor: `AS referred_by`, `AS rows_per_key`, `AS late_loans`, the VALUES list of the rota CTE, ORDER BY of the FULL JOIN query.
issues.fixLooksLike: Re-break so the operative part sits inside ~40 columns: put the correlated `WHERE l.member_id = m.member_id` on its own indented line in both EXISTS subqueries and break the NOT IN subquery after `NOT IN (`; put `ON` on its own line under each LEFT JOIN in the fix query and split the `owes` expression over two lines; one SELECT item per line where the list is long. Shorten result headers so panels fit 40 columns (alias `p.payment_id AS pay_id`, or drop `m.name` since the WHERE fixes it to Ada; alias the NULL demo columns `eq_11, eq_1n, eq_nn, n_is_n` or stack them as two queries). In C#: one `new(...)` per line, break the LeftJoin signature after the return type, move the comment above a shorter `if`, break `left.Join(` before each argument. Re-run run-code and verify-page and check mobile parts 10-17.

issues.location: Anti-joins, paragraph beginning 'It returns nothing, and Dalia has still borrowed nothing' (article line 734; mobile-dark part16, desktop-light part11-12).
issues.problem: The densest paragraph on the page (13 lines on a phone) carries two long inline-code expansions, `4 NOT IN (1, 1, 2, 3, NULL)` and the 50-character `4 <> 1 AND ... AND 4 <> NULL`, which wrap across three lines mid-expression on mobile and two on desktop. The brief says long expansions go in a block, not inline. This is also the most dangerous bug in the article and it is presented as ordinary body text while the milder forgotten-ON case gets the page's only pitfall callout.
issues.fixLooksLike: Lift the expansion into a short fenced `text` block (the NOT IN form, the AND chain one comparison per line, the NULL verdict) and split the paragraph in two around it (mechanism; then the PostgreSQL quote and the NOT EXISTS conclusion). Consider making the NOT IN explanation a :::pitfall; two pitfalls in a 22-minute page is still restrained.

issues.location: Sources list (front matter lines 45-64; desktop-light part14, mobile-dark part20) versus the body.
issues.problem: Five of the fourteen listed sources are never referred to in the body: both MySQL 8.4 pages (MySQL is not mentioned anywhere in the article), the T-SQL IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM page, and the two PostgreSQL planner/operator-optimization pages (the join-algorithm section attributes only to SQLite and SQL Server). The brief treats a listed-but-uncited source as a finding. Separately, in-prose attributions ('the PostgreSQL manual', 'SQLite's manual') are plain text, and with five PostgreSQL and four SQLite entries in an unkeyed list a reader cannot tell which page backs which sentence.
issues.fixLooksLike: Either cite each of the five where it supports a claim (for example one sentence on MySQL's `<=>` and SQL Server 2022's IS NOT DISTINCT FROM next to the PostgreSQL/SQLite spellings; PostgreSQL's planner page beside the hash/merge bullets) or remove them from front matter. Make each in-prose attribution a Markdown link to the exact page, as WRITER_GUIDE section on links allows.

issues.location: NOT IN query result panel (article lines 729-732; desktop-light part11, mobile-dark part16).
issues.problem: The empty result renders as a header and a rule with nothing under it, which at a glance looks like a truncated or broken panel rather than 'zero rows'. The zero-row result is the whole point of the example.
